events.title: The Holy Roman Empire Comes to an End
events.description: Emperor Francis II abdicated the imperial crown and released the empire's states from their obligations. This ended an institution that had existed in some form for roughly a thousand years. Francis II kept the title Emperor of Austria, which he had taken in 1804.
events.significance: The abdication closed a chapter of European history that began in the Middle Ages. It also cleared the way for a new German political order in the 19th century.

events.title: Bolivia Declares Independence
events.description: Delegates meeting in Chuquisaca proclaimed Bolivia's independence from Spanish rule. The country took the name of the liberator Simón Bolívar.
events.significance: The declaration was one of the last major steps in the South American wars of independence. Bolivia still celebrates August 6 as its national day.

events.title: Atomic Bomb Dropped on Hiroshima
events.description: At 8:16 a.m., the American B-29 Enola Gay dropped the bomb known as Little Boy on the Japanese city of Hiroshima. It was the first use of a nuclear weapon in warfare. Tens of thousands of people died at once, and many more died in the months that followed.
events.significance: The bombing changed warfare and global politics and helped bring World War II to a close. It also began the nuclear age and the long debate over nuclear weapons. Hiroshima marks the anniversary each year with a peace ceremony.

events.title: Jamaica Gains Independence
events.description: Jamaica became an independent nation within the Commonwealth after more than 300 years of British rule. The Caribbean island had been under British control since 1655.
events.significance: Independence made Jamaica a sovereign state, and it has celebrated August 6 as Independence Day ever since. It was part of the wave of decolonization that reshaped Africa and the Caribbean in the mid-20th century.

events.title: Voting Rights Act Signed into Law
events.description: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The law enforced the 14th and 15th Amendments and targeted the discriminatory practices that had kept many Black Americans from voting.
events.significance: It is one of the most important civil rights laws in American history. Black voter registration rose sharply in the years after it passed.
